A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HMSCs are able to promote the nerve regeneration in a neurotmesis rat model, by acting through paraxine mechanisms.

, although HMSCs are not able to promote a better regeneration of the injured sciatic nerve in the neurotmetic injury rat model, they can be considered as a potential source of bioactive molecules for nerve regeneration.

HMSCs, when associated with a PLC membrane, can be used as an effective tool for peripheral nerve regeneration, especially in cases of nerve injuries where the end-to-end sute or nerve grafting is not feasible.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of HMSCs to the repair site of the injured peripheral nerve does not seem to be effective in improving the functional recovery of the injured nerve.

HMSCs are able to differentiate into neuroglial cells in vitro, and their employment in a nerve injury model can be beneficial in terms of motor function recovery, but the effect is not evident in terms of sensory and autonomic function recovery.

HMSCs, associated to a PLC membrane, may be a useful tool for the regeneration of peripheral nerves, especially in case of a neurotmesis, when the surgical reconstruction of the nerve is not feasible.
